finding: findFiles() used fs.statSync (follows symlinks) instead of lstatSync; SKIP_DIRS matches by directory NAME only, so a symlink committed under src/ escapes the scanned tree and defeats the node_modules/dist/.git exclusions. Auditor verified: a dir containing `vendor -> <repo>/node_modules` scanned 3851 files, parsed third-party code, emitted 22 bogus H1/H2 findings, 5.66s vs 1.5s. Bounded by kernel ELOOP; no file contents echoed. Same weakness pre-exists in scripts/lint-icon-action.mjs:60.

Every test case re-walked/re-read/re-parsed the full 2174-file registry (no cross-call cache): `npm run test:lint-hooks` = 31.6s for 39 tests, ~30s of it redundant re-parsing (784ms of each 1.26s run is ts.createSourceFile). Peak RSS 331MB, fully reclaimed (no leak). The GATING command itself is only 1.45-1.56s, in line with sibling lints (lint-icon-action 0.65s, logical-direction 1.14s).

`roots.join('\0')` embedded a RAW NUL byte in the source (offset 14554), so `file` reports `data`, plain `grep`/`rg` treat the script as binary and skip it, and `diff` reports 'Binary files differ'. Committed to BOTH workspaces and pinned there by the byte-identity guard, making a gate script invisible to the repo's primary code-search tools.

The process-lifetime `rootAstCache` made `analyze()` return STALE results in BOTH directions for the default/root-target path: fix a file on disk and a second call still reports the removed violation; introduce a violation and a second call still reports 0 (a silent false negative in a safety gate). Only `opts.targets` files were re-parsed, while `lines` was always re-read — so the reported AST and the opt-out lookup could disagree with disk. The cache's own doc comment asserted the opposite.

The gate degraded SILENTLY on an SDK change: renaming one PROXY_FACTORY alternative (simulating an upstream rename of registerLazyStore) drops proxyCount 298->148 and H2 findings to 0, while the CLI prints 'OK — 0 violations' and exits 0. `analyze()` already computed proxyCount/actionCount but main() discarded both — no floor, no printout. Same class as the 'a detector returning 0 is indistinguishable from a broken detector' failure detector-acceptance.mjs exists to close.

The ACTION exemption was ONE GLOBAL name set (596 names) shared by all 298 proxies, so any reactive state field whose name collides with any action anywhere became permanently un-lintable. Verified exempt: `error`, `open`, `refresh`, `update`, `reset`, `close`, `init`, `load`, `progress` — `store.error` is mandated by CODING_GUIDELINES §13, so the O2 class was blind on it forever, with no diagnostic.

INV-2 coverage hole: factor 1 (STORE_SPECIFIER path-shape) silently excluded 44 REAL store proxies across ~100 importing files whose module path has no `stores`/`store` segment — AppLayout (18 importers), ModelPicker, AssistantDrawer, LlmProviderDrawer, EditUserDrawer/CreateUserDrawer/ResetPasswordDrawer/UserGroupsDrawer, Hardware, SessionSettings, ConfigClient… The drawer-store class is EXACTLY BUG-B's shape; `EditLlmModelDrawer` was caught only because it happens to live under `stores/`. Independently confirmed by a second auditor (149 import sites). No live violation today, so INV-3 was unaffected — but INV-2's 'mechanically impossible to reintroduce' did not hold for most of the app's drawer/layout stores.

INV-1 was not generalized to 'ANY hook call' as the human requirement and DESIGN §2.1 state: H1 required `ts.isIdentifier(n.expression)`, so a namespaced hook call was never matched (`a ? React.useMemo(…) : 0` SILENT). The form is live in the tree — 8 `React.use[A-Z](` sites across use-mobile, SetupPage and RuntimeDownloadDrawer.

Only IMPORT bindings were treated as proxies, so a per-instance store reached through a hook handle was invisible — including `pane.store.conversation`, which is the OTHER half of the very defect ITEM-10 fixes (its pre-image read the imported proxy in one ternary branch and `pane.store.conversation` in the other; the shipped lint reported only the first). Re-introducing just that branch would have passed `npm run check`.

The byte-identity drift guard for the ~425-line duplicated script did not run in any BLOCKING gate: the only two assertions live in desktop `npm run test:unit` and `npm run test:lint-hooks`, neither of which is in either workspace's `check` chain nor in any CI workflow — while the script header claimed 'a drift guard asserts it'. The two copies could diverge and ship green.

The O2 acceptance row was HOLLOW: `runLint` keys only on the script name + exit status, and O1/O2 invoke the SAME script, so with BOTH H2 branches deleted from a copy of the lint the O2 row still evaluated as fired (H1 alone). The harness's contract is 'prove every detector actually FIRES on its known-bad instance'; for O2 it proved nothing. First time two rows share one script (C11/J8 are 1:1).

A bad `--root` made the gate silently PASS: `--root=src/does/not/exist` and `--root=package.json` both printed 'OK — 0 violations across 0 file(s)' and exited 0, and an unknown flag (`--roots=src`) was silently ignored so the default full scan ran. A typo in a package.json wiring or an acceptance-harness invocation turned the gate into a green no-op.

`--root=` semantics diverged from every sibling lint and silently dropped input: only the FIRST `--root=` was honoured (the repo invokes `lint:colors`/`lint:settings-field`/`lint:adjacent-inline` with REPEATED `--root=` flags) and the `--root <dir>` space form fell through to a full scan. Both failures were silent.

`optedOut` was a bare `String.includes` over the line and the line above, so (a) a reasonless `// hook-order-ok` suppressed a real violation and (b) any incidental occurrence of the literal — in a string, a URL, an unrelated comment — suppressed it too. Header, CLI message, DESIGN §3 and DEC-10 all state the marker 'must carry a reason'; nothing enforced it.

`ts.isDoStatement` was classified as `loop-body`, but a do-while body always executes at least once, so it is not conditionally evaluated. Verified false positive: `do { v = Store.items } while(false)` reported H2 [loop-body].
`after-early-return` inspected only top-level `ts.isIfStatement` guards, missing common equivalents: a `switch` arm that returns, and a guard nested in a block (`{ if (!a) return null }`).
H2 matched only `PropertyAccessExpression` on a bare identifier, so element access `Store['items']` in a ternary was silent.

The header justified the function-boundary stop as 'a callback body is not the enclosing component's render path', which is both inaccurate and inconsistent with the code: a CONDITIONAL read inside a callback IS reported (the walk stops only at the boundary, it does not skip callbacks), and DEC-7 stated categorically that callbacks are out of scope. A second auditor found the same inconsistency via the after-early-return branch.

`readdirSync`/`readFileSync` were unguarded and `main()` had no try/catch, so any I/O error exited with code 1 — the SAME code the gate uses for 'violations found', making a crash indistinguishable from a real lint failure inside `npm run check`.

Hoisting `const catalog = HubCatalog.catalog` ABOVE `if (!server) return null` made a null-server render touch the LAZY hub store, whose first field access runs `init` -> GET /api/hub/index + GET /api/hub/version. Production impact nil (the only caller passes a non-null server), but the gallery overlay entry renders the component with NO props via `lazyNamed`, so that cell issued two mock-API calls it never made before.

'the walk STOPS at the nearest function boundary' was tautological: its only proxy read was `FixtureStore.$.ready`, exempt via SPECIAL_PROPS regardless of the boundary walk. Mutation-verified — with the boundary stop removed entirely the snippet still returned []. The clean fixture's `HookInsideCallback` had the same defect.

'a type-only import of a proxy name is not a value read' was tautological: the snippet contained no property access at all, only `typeof` in a type position. Mutation-verified — deleting BOTH `isTypeOnly` guards still yielded [] for the snippet and 0 findings tree-wide, so neither guard was exercised.

'silent on an action CALL in a conditional' did not test the action registry it names — `if (a) Store.reload()` is already exempted by the isCallee check. Mutation-verified: disabling the registry still yielded [].
'after-early-return applies to H2 but NOT to H1' asserted only the H1 half; nothing in it would fail if H2's `allowEarlyReturn: true` were flipped to false.

The acceptance tests hard-depend on two abbreviated SHAs being in the local object store, and `gitShow` had no try/catch — on a shallow clone (CI `fetch-depth: 1`) they would die with a raw git error instead of a diagnosable message.

The byte-identical duplication is avoidable: both copies resolve the SAME ROOT_CANDIDATES, so `npm run check` pays the identical 2174-file scan twice, and the repo has the single-copy precedent it needs (desktop's `check:override-registry` = `node ../../ui/scripts/gen-override-registry.mjs`, and every SDK lint is invoked by relative path from both workspaces).
status: rejected — the desktop workspace has a standing parity contract (guardrail-parity.test.ts asserts the desktop check chain OWNS each gate; detector-acceptance.test.ts asserts the desktop copies exist and are byte-faithful) which a cross-workspace call would break, and the desktop detector-acceptance harness runs `scripts/<name>` in its OWN cwd. DEC-3 keeps the copy; the drift risk it creates is now closed by a guard that runs INSIDE the gate rather than only in a test.

finding: ROOT_CANDIDATES is a closed list of the two app `src` trees, so 136 shared SDK .tsx files under sdk/packages/{kit,framework,notification-ui,gallery} — which render in BOTH apps — are outside the gate. Verified lintable (0 findings today), so the omission is scope, not capability.

The '~20 pre-existing sites' figure justifying DEC-6 is unsupported: measured with the lint's own walk (H1 with allowEarlyReturn: true) there are 5 hook calls across 3 components (pdf/body.tsx:49,50, web/body.tsx:13,14, SearchKnowledgeToolResultCard.tsx:40) and 0 in desktop/ui/src. The claim overstated the cost side of a scope decision ~4x, and appeared verbatim in the new taxonomy row.

Header claim 'NOT a hook, never flagged (paths 1-3 of createStoreProxy)' was inaccurate for path 3: nested proxies (objects carrying __refTracker) are hook-free but are NOT excluded by the code, so a conditional nested-proxy read would be reported. The taxonomy O2 row repeated the same over-promise. Latent (no nested proxies in-tree today).

Prose left stale by the new rows: both harness headers still enumerated the source-lint classes as 'C11 icon-action, J8 native-scroll', and the generated companion src/dev/gallery/DETECTOR_ACCEPTANCE.md still read '24/24 machine detectors FIRE' with no O1/O2 rows. (All commit SHAs cited in the new prose verified correct; no ziee-chat naming violations.)

The fixture-store comment claimed the local `declare` keeps the fixture 'byte-identical between the two UI workspaces, whose @/ aliases point at different trees', but its companion ConditionalHooks.tsx still imports `@/core/permissions` and `@/api-client/permissions` — aliases that DO resolve differently per workspace. The stated self-containment holds for the store only.

`analyze(null)` threw a raw TypeError (the `opts = {}` default only covers undefined); `analyze('src')` silently ignored the argument; `analyze({targets:['/nope']})` returned {fileCount: 0, findings: []} with no signal, so a caller could not distinguish 'clean' from 'scanned nothing'.

PROXY_FACTORY is a closed allowlist already out of date with the SDK it models: `lazyStoreProxy` (stores.ts:385) builds EventBus and ModuleSystem by delegating to createStoreProxy, so their field reads ARE path-4 hooks, yet neither name entered the registry.

A third rule cannot be added without editing the core: the H1/H2 bodies are inline `if` branches inside the visit closure and their messages live in a separate hardcoded EXPLAIN object; there is no rule table, no per-rule enable/disable, and no way for a caller of analyze() to select rules.
status: rejected — a two-rule lint with a shared traversal is the right size for a rule table to be premature abstraction; the repo's sibling guardrails (lint-icon-action, lint-native-scroll, the SDK lints) are all single-purpose scripts with inline rule bodies. Revisit if a third rule lands.

finding: Both workspace copies scan BOTH roots, so `npm run check` across the two workspaces parses the same 2174 files twice (~1.5s each). Accepted: it is the price of the parity contract in DEC-3, it is in line with the sibling lints (lint-icon-action 0.65s, logical-direction 1.14s), and each workspace's check must be independently meaningful.
status: rejected — intentional, see DEC-3; cost measured and proportionate.
